description: Key chain connector - carrier and cluster boards
notes: DECIDED 2026-09-21. Pinout GND SCK GND SH/LD GND SER GND QH GND 3V3 spare spare - a ground between every signal (ADR 0001 item 1). EIGHT of them, not five: the chain is four hops and SER/QH are point-to-point rather than bus, so every cluster board but the last carries an IN and an OUT. Carrier 1, right_thumb 2, right_hand 2, left_thumb 2, left_hand 1, with four ribbon assemblies between. BOXED AND KEYED because a reversed chain connector puts 3V3 into QH. Same pinout at all eight | 2026-09-21: SHROUD HEIGHT ESTABLISHED from genuine vendor datasheets now in the repo - 9.10 +/-0.15mm above the board (Wurth WR-BHD, datasheets/connectors/WR-BHD-61201621621.pdf) or 9.3 +/-0.25mm (3M 303 series, datasheets/connectors/3M-303-SERIES-BOXED-HEADER.pdf), against a 20mm cavity. A review's measured ~8.9mm was right to within 0.2-0.4mm. TWO THINGS FOLLOW. 3M's 303 length table has NO 12-pin entry (06/08/10/14/16/20/26/34/36/40/50), so a 2x6 must come from Wurth or another vendor - Wurth's 2x6 is 22.90mm long (L = pin-to-pin + 10.20). And the number that actually decides 'tight' is the MATED stack height, which is STILL BLOCKED: no ribbon-socket datasheet exists in any indexed repo, so the socket sit-height and the ribbon bend are not established | *** 2026-09-21 THE MATED STACK HEIGHT IS NO LONGER BLOCKED, AND THE CAVITY IS NOT TIGHT. *** TE Connectivity Catalog 82012, 'Ribbon Cable Interconnect Solutions', Revised 10-09, 104pp, banked at datasheets/connectors/TE-IDC-SOCKET-CATALOG-82012.pdf. Page 52, 622/636 series female socket, dimensions verified by rendering the page (the drawing is vector, pdftotext returns nothing): socket height BEFORE crimping 14.10 (.555); AFTER crimping WITHOUT strain relief 10.5 (.413) with 12.10 (.476) MAX; AFTER crimping WITH strain relief 14.35 (.565) / 16.8 (.661); body width 6.10 (.240) MAX. Corroborated at p.54 by the 609 series, 12.37 before / 10.54 after. ARITHMETIC, and the assumption it rests on: H_mated = H_header + H_socket - D_cavity, which assumes the socket bottoms on the cavity floor. Against the Wurth header (9.10mm shroud, 6.50mm cavity): 9.10 + 10.50 - 6.50 = 13.10mm nominal, 14.70mm with the 12.10 MAX socket. Against the 3M (9.30mm): 13.30 / 14.90mm. *** SO 13.1-14.9mm INTO A 20mm CAVITY - 5.1mm OF SPARE IN THE WORST CASE, AND 13.10mm IS A HARD LOWER BOUND REGARDLESS OF THE ASSUMPTION, since insertion depth cannot exceed cavity depth. *** DO NOT FIT A STRAIN-RELIEF CLIP: it takes the stack to 16.95mm nominal and 19.60mm worst case, i.e. 0.4mm of clearance. TE's 622 table at p.53 does not offer one at 12 positions anyway (P/N 2-1658527-0, A 19.74, B 12.70, C 3.81), which is the same thin 2x6 coverage found on the 3M header side. THIRD VENDOR CONFIRMING THE HEADER SHROUD: TE's own low-profile header at p.76 is .388 [9.86] above board including a 1.04mm standoff, 0.6-0.8mm taller than the Wurth and 3M parts. STILL NOT-IN-DOCUMENT: the cable exit and ribbon bend height, so the ribbon's own turn radius remains uncounted

description: Fuse on the 3V3 conductor feeding the cluster boards
notes: PROPOSED by carrier.md and never given a row until 2026-09-21. The 3V3 conductor runs 265mm through the body beside 12V LED power; a short on it browns out the dev board LDO and takes the instrument down with no diagnosis. Two millimetres of board, unretrofittable | *** 2026-09-21: THE TRIP POINT IS NOT THE PROBLEM, THE SERIES RESISTANCE IS. *** Bourns MF-PSMF010X (datasheets/discrete-and-power/MF-PSMF010X-polyfuse.pdf, banked as the nearest available part): Ihold 0.10A, Itrip 0.30A, Vmax 15V, max time-to-trip 0.5s at 1.5A - all fine. But RESISTANCE IS 1.0 TO 7.5 OHMS at 23C, which at the FUSE'S 100mA HOLD CURRENT would be 0.1 to 0.75V of drop - *** BUT THAT IS THE WRONG CURRENT AND THIS ROW OVERSTATED IT 3.9x. *** The circuit draws 25.8mA (18 closed keys at 1.43mA), so the real drop is 26 to 194 mV [calc: 7.5 x 0.0258]. And it is harmless for a reason the objection missed: the 74HC165's thresholds and the key pull-ups sit on the SAME rail, so the RC crossing time is independent of VCC and key-release-time does not move. OBJECTION WITHDRAWN on the voltage drop into a 3V3 rail whose stated failure mode is browning out the dev-board LDO. The fuse would cause the fault it exists to prevent, at the top of its tolerance band. ALSO THE PACKAGE IS WRONG: this part is 0805, this row says 1206. RE-OPEN THIS DECISION: either a much lower-resistance part, or accept the unfused conductor, or move the protection to the source end where the drop lands on nothing | 2026-09-21: PACKAGE COLUMN CORRECTED to 0805. The row's own notes already said 0805 and the column still said 1206 - the correction landed in the prose and not in the field, which is this project's named failure mode inside a single row | 2026-09-21: DATASHEET PATH CORRECTED. This row cited the banked file without its -polyfuse suffix, so the path resolved to nothing. It was the only dangling datasheets/ path in the whole corpus, and no tool could see it: verify-datasheets.py checks the manifest against the disk, never the corpus against the manifest

description: Selects the 74HC165 serial-input source on each cluster board
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/cluster/cluster-boards.md. Position A on the three boards that have an OUT connector: SER comes from the next board's QH. Position B on the chain-end board: SER comes from the IN pin 6 passthrough, which reaches the carrier. One link is what lets all four boards be ONE schematic instead of a special last variant

description: Pull-up on the chain-end board serial input
notes: PROPOSED by hardware/cluster/cluster-boards.md. Chain-end board only. Holds the far serial input high when nothing drives it, which is the tied-off case ADR 0001 specified. If firmware instead DRIVES it from the carrier's IO33, the 100R series wins against 10k to within 33mV of the rail - so an end-to-end chain self-test (shift a known pattern through all 32 bits, distinguishing a broken loom from a stuck bit) becomes a FIRMWARE choice rather than a board choice, for one resistor
